edr-bot: ALERT: High-confidence detection id=EDR-2026-87: suspicious crypto-miner process 'xmrig.exe' spawning on host MIA-2026 (Windows 10). CPU spike 87%. File quarantined: C:\Users\mia\AppData\Local\Temp\tjd3x.exe. Network connections to 45.77.12.5:3333. Link: https://edr.redwood.internal/alerts/EDR-2026-87 :eyes:

mia (IR): I'm seeing the popup on my laptop, I'm working from home right now. Notified. Laptop is personal network.

alex (eng-security): Thanks. Can you confirm serial/asset tag and whether you were on VPN or using any cloud credentials locally? Also hit the machine off the network if possible (unplug wifi) to avoid any exfil.

mia (IR): Asset tag RW-5492, serial S/N 9X4-SS12. I was not on VPN, but I had AWS CLI open earlier.

jordan (it-support): Okay I can remote into the machine for a live response if Mia is okay. Mia, can you keep it powered on but disconnected from internet? We'll pull in a support session.

kyle (sre): Alex / eng-sec: flagging potential blast radius — rotate any tokens that may have been used from that host (AWS keys, GitHub PATs, local dev certs). Also check CI/CD runs in last 24h for odd commits.

alex (eng-security): Agreed. Immediate containment steps: 1) isolate device via EDR console (done by edr-bot). 2) collect live artifacts: process list, scheduled tasks, autoruns, network connections, memory image if possible. 3) rotate any credentials used from the host. 4) image or reprovision after confirm.

edr-bot: ACTION: device isolated from network at 1764823008. Process 'xmrig.exe' killed. Quarantine hash: SHA256=3f7b8c9e2d4a5c8d1a1b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f

alex (eng-security): Jordan — please run the following live response commands and paste outputs:
```
erdctl edr live-cli --device MIA-2026 --collect process-list netstat autoruns scheduled-tasks
```
Also run:
```
certutil -hashfile C:\Users\mia\AppData\Local\Temp\tjd3x.exe SHA256
```

jordan (it-support): Running now, will paste results. Mia, can you confirm you have no personal files open?

mia (IR): Nothing important open. Good to go.

jordan (it-support): process-list: xmrig.exe (pid 8420) parent explorer.exe. netstat: outbound TCP to 45.77.12.5:3333. autoruns: none matching. scheduled-tasks: none. certutil returned SHA256: 3f7b8c9e2d4a5c8d1a1b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f

alex (eng-security): Good. Create incident INC-2026-45. Triage notes: likely commodity miner delivered via malicious MSI/packer in temp. No persistence indicators in scheduled tasks/autoruns but need full disk scan and memory dump to be safe.

kyle (sre): I'll scan logs for access to any service principals created from that host IP and look for suspicious deploys or key creation.

jordan (it-support): Starting full EDR scan + memory capture. ETA ~12 minutes. Also grabbing browser history and recent downloads.

alex (eng-security): While scan runs: rotate all tokens that Mia used: AWS keys, GitHub, DockerHub keys. If any SSH private keys stored locally, revoke and reissue. Update the audit log with rotated keys actions.

mia (IR): I will rotate my AWS keys and GitHub PAT now.

edr-bot: UPDATE: full scan completed at 1764823130. No further malware found. Memory image uploaded to /forensics/inc-2026-45/mia-memory-1764823130.img.

jordan (it-support): Memory dump shows command line: "xmrig.exe -o 45.77.12.5:3333 -u wallet.xxxx" and parent process spawned from temp. No evidence of lateral tools.

alex (eng-security): Ok, recommended remediation: 1) reprovision laptop (wipe & reinstall), 2) restore from known-good backup only, 3) reissue all creds, 4) monitor infra for suspicious access from affected keys. Also add a 7-day follow-up scan and 30-day detection watch.

mia (IR): I'm fine with reprovision. Jordan — can you schedule the wipe and send checklist?

jordan (it-support): Scheduling now. Wipe tomorrow 09:00 PST. Checklist: backup personal files to secure share, enroll device in MDM after reinstall, install EDR agent, rotate credentials, send confirmation to this thread.

kyle (sre): I'll watch for suspicious CI/CD activity and create alerts for any usage of rotated keys.

alex (eng-security): Post-incident actions: open PR to add miner YARA signatures to EDR, add detection for outbound to 45.77.12.5:3333, add runbook step to rotate cloud creds when an endpoint with cloud tooling is compromised. Assigning to eng-security backlog.

jordan (it-support): Done. Incident INC-2026-45 created, owner @alex. Wipe scheduled.

mia (IR): Confirmed AWS & GitHub tokens rotated. Will report when reprovision done. :thumbsup: 

alex (eng-security): Nice. Closing preliminary containment. Leave incident open for root cause and follow-up. Add note: no evidence of data exfil at this time.

edr-bot: NOTE: follow-up scheduled scan in 7 days (1765427800). If green, incident will be moved to monitoring state.

kyle (sre): Quick reminder — check KMS access logs and audit logs for key usage from that host; rotate keys if there's any unexpected sign.

alex (eng-security): Will do. Thanks everyone for the quick response.

mia (IR): Appreciate it, team.
